correctness.rationale: The labeled Petersen graph is KG(5,2), 10 vertices and 15 edges; each of 2^15=32,768 masks encodes exactly one edge orientation. Kahn's algorithm identifies precisely 16,680 acyclic masks, and a source or sink at any vertex generates exactly the legal three-bit toggles. Independently constructed the whole click adjacency graph and all 704 components, with complete size multiplicities 12:120,16:120,21:120,22:120,28:120,38:60,50:24,66:20, satisfying Σ s c_s=16,680. BFS from each state in its component gives exact diameter counts 480 diameter-5 / 224 diameter-6, 13,880 eccentricity-5 / 2,800 eccentricity-6 orientations, and unordered pair distance histogram d=1..6 (28,140,50,400,63,040,60,960,30,500,2,040), sum 235,080=Σ c_s binom(s,2). Independently built all 5!=120 S5 graph-automorphism permutations, mapped full components, found nine component orbits sizes 120,120,60,60,120,120,60,24,20 with precisely the two size-21 orbits exchanged by global arrow reversal. The five maximum independent sets of size four identify S5 as full automorphism group. All finite cases enumerated exhaustively, not sampled; source script and distinct independent reconstruction inspect all orientation masks and BFS distances.

originality.rationale: Prior Macauley–Mortveit theory and Petersen Tutte/chromatic polynomials imply 704 click classes and 16,680 acyclic orientations: both totals are acknowledged *not novel*. Cameron computed 168 automorphism orbits on individual orientations, distinct from nine orbits on components. The published Resultary general all-graph flex theorem yields the metric median-potential formula, so general distance *principles* are also prior; however it does not contain the exact Petersen size/diameter strata, orbit split, reversal pairing or full numerical distance histogram. This is an independently complete census of a canonical graph, not a new universal flip theorem. An earlier unindexed census or table with the same strata is a residual priority risk.

The median-potential shortest path theory is prior and must not be claimed as new.
